A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, algorithms, equations and Appendices A–C are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original synthetic experiments. Figures 1 and 2 show likelihood trajectories, test errors and likelihood distributions from training and post-training.

after.justification: V2 retains the original synthetic experiments and adds an original evaluation of Qwen3-8B-Base and Qwen3-8B on Math-500, reported in Figure 2a.

M1.justification: The PG-OR/PG-PR updates, adaptive learning rates and best-of-m exploration are retained. Algorithm 2 makes the base/uniform sampling mixture explicit, while the new Section 3.1 footnote explains prediction-query reuse within the existing exploration framework.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only synthetic mixture and hypercube tasks. V2 retains these and adds mathematical reasoning on the 500-problem Math-500 benchmark using actual language models, substantially extending coverage beyond synthetic linear models.

E2.justification: The proposed PG experiments retain the outcome-reward versus process-reward comparison. The new Qwen3 base/post-trained comparison illustrates likelihood quantiles separately; neither model is evaluated as a competing method against the proposed PG algorithms.

E3.justification: The added Math-500 evaluation uses two 8B models, 64 completions per problem, temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95 and top-k 50. This introduces a new generation-based evaluation protocol; the retained synthetic experiments have unchanged reported settings.

E4.justification: Figure 2a adds a real-model diagnostic case study of the base-model barrier through likelihood-quantile curves before and after post-training. The synthetic off-support and training-trajectory analyses remain; no new component ablations or sensitivity studies appear.

E5.justification: Section 6 adds statistical estimation of per-problem success probability using the fraction of correct answers among 64 completions, whereas the retained synthetic curves use directly computed model likelihoods. No confidence intervals, significance tests or training-seed variability are added.

E6.justification: Figure 2a adds Qwen3 likelihood-quantile results: both models have lower-tail estimated zeros, the post-trained model is higher through much of the middle range, and the curves cross toward the upper range. The synthetic results are retained without changed findings or values.

T1.justification: Assumption 1 now bounds features for all sequences, and new Assumption 2 strengthens Corollary 7's conditions. Theorems 10–12 and Appendix C substantially revise hard-instance constructions, parameter restrictions and lower bounds. Theorem 11's mistake bound changes from Omega(k^N/gamma^2) to Omega(k^N/(N gamma^2)); Theorem 12 restricts outputs to autoregressive linear models and uses new Lemma 28. Appendix A also changes Proposition 20's min to max and adds a zeta-squared factor to Corollary 24's reward-query bound.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 narrows the explicit minimax-optimality contribution from the methods in Sections 3 and 4 to those in Section 3, withdrawing the corresponding claim for process-reward PG. The central base-model-barrier and adaptive-SGD claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly interprets the Qwen3 curves as suggesting that post-training did not extend the base model's support. Appendix A.6 removes the claim that clipping affects only iteration complexity under best-of-m exploration, consistent with the revised reward-query bound. Existing concluding limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new evaluation's model identities, completion count, likelihood estimator and decoding parameters, and clarifies online query reuse. Synthetic implementation settings and the code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Qwen3 technical report and Let's Verify Step by Step in connection with the new experiment. Most other reference edits update publication metadata or authorship; the substantive related-work positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The section and appendix organization remains stable. V2 adds an experimental paragraph and explanatory footnote, locally rewrites proof passages, and corrects wording, notation and bibliographic details without broadly restructuring the narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 2 replaces the synthetic CDF panel with the Qwen3 comparison, retains the synthetic quantile panel, and adds panel labels, a model legend and a revised caption. Figure 1 is visually unchanged; the remaining layout differences mainly reflect text reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important gaps in the paper's core theory. Appendix C replaces position-independent constructions used for arbitrary target sequences with constructions that explicitly support the margin condition, while Assumption 2 supplies conditions needed for Corollary 7's equal-token-likelihood argument. Together with corrected complexity bounds, these substantially improve theoretical reliability despite narrower guarantees. The Math-500 illustration adds practical context, although zero successes among 64 completions cannot establish zero probability or unchanged support.
